Working with **film-crew** (single-shot mode) and then **cinema-worldbuilder-pro-2.0**, the skill for Kling. I didn't do the usual session-start pull because this folder isn't a git repo, and there's no NOTES.md, so I have no open items to report.

**What the crew decided (single shot):**
- **Director:** The shot is about patience. An old craft lives on in a city that has rebuilt itself, and the light is the only witness. He shows nothing on his face; the whole performance is in his hands.
- **Set and costume:** Gyumri's dark, rust-veined tuff stone walls, a deep arched window, and a scarred walnut workbench. He is carving a pomegranate pattern into a walnut panel. He's about 75 and wears a grey flat cap, a charcoal wool vest and a worn leather apron.
- **Camera and light:** A 35mm lens at eye level. The only key light is one low amber sunset beam from the window, and the rest of the room is in cool blue-grey shade. The look is a warm, filmic tungsten-film style, described in words without naming any brand.
- **Camera move:** One slow, steady orbit of about 90°. It starts on a three-quarter front view and ends on his profile, with the window beam behind him lighting the dust from behind.
- **Sound:** Only sounds from the room, with no music and no speech.

**Assumptions:**
- No reference images, so this is text-to-video.
- The carving is a pomegranate pattern.
- The camera turns clockwise.
- Kling 3.0 has an 8 s option. If yours doesn't, choose 10 s; the action still fits.
- Audio: if your Kling 3.0 has the native-audio switch on, it will follow the sound sentence in the prompt. If not, add the sounds from the sound note in editing.

**Risks:**
- Hands holding tools are the usual weak spot. The negative prompt names those problems directly.
- If the orbit overshoots 90°, regenerate rather than editing the prompt.

## FINAL

**Video prompt — Kling 3.0, 8 s, 16:9**

**Settings:** Kling 3.0 · Text-to-Video · 8 s (10 s if 8 isn't offered) · 16:9 · Professional / High quality · Creativity/CFG left at default (≈0.5) · Native audio ON if available · 1 output

**Prompt:**
```
One continuous 8-second cinematic shot, no cuts, real-time motion. Dusk inside an old woodcarving workshop in Gyumri, Armenia: thick walls of dark black-and-rust volcanic tuff stone, one small deep-set arched window, a heavy scarred walnut workbench, chisels and gouges racked on the wall, pale wood shavings curled on the stone floor, no readable text anywhere.

An elderly Armenian master woodcarver, about 75, deep-lined weathered face, short white stubble, grey flat cap, faded charcoal wool vest over a collarless shirt with rolled sleeves, worn brown leather apron, thick knuckled hands, sits at the bench carving a pomegranate ornament into a walnut panel with a steel gouge and a round wooden mallet. His face stays calm and focused, eyes on the wood; all the emotion lives in his hands.

Opening frame: medium shot from his front-left three-quarter side at eye level, the warm window beam raking across his hands and the carving. A single low shaft of amber sunset light cuts through the dim room; fine sawdust and dust motes drift and glitter inside the beam, while the rest of the workshop falls into cool blue-grey shadow.

Action: he taps the mallet against the gouge three times in a slow, unhurried rhythm, each tap lifting a small puff of sawdust into the light. Then he sets the mallet down and blows gently across the carving, and a soft cloud of fine dust swirls up and hangs glowing in the beam.

Camera: a slow, smooth, constant-speed orbit of about 90 degrees around him, clockwise, steady like a dolly on a curved track, distance unchanged, horizon level, no shake, no zoom.

Last frame: his side profile in medium close-up, the window now behind him, his face and cap edged in warm rim light, the glowing dust cloud backlit between him and the window, the finished curve of the pomegranate carving sharp in the foreground; he sits still, looking at his work.

Look: 35mm lens, moderate shallow depth of field, focus held on his hands and face, warm amber key against cool shadows, soft film grain, rich natural skin texture, gentle highlight roll-off, photoreal.

Sound: only the room — dry wooden knocks of the mallet, the scrape of the gouge biting walnut, a soft breath blowing dust, faint distant city evening hum through the window. No music, no speech.
```

**Negative prompt:**
```
morphing hands, extra or missing fingers, tool passing through hand, floating chisel, warped mallet, melting face, face distortion, jump cut, scene change, camera shake, fast camera, zoom, slow motion, oversaturated, cartoon, CGI look, text, letters, watermark, logo, subtitles, music
```

**Sound note** (for editing, only if native audio is off): add 3 dry mallet knocks with the gouge scraping under them, then a soft breath, over a faint evening city hum. Use no music.
